chapter_structure.label_ar: الفصل الأول: الأجنبي القادم من الخارج
chapter_structure.title_ar: دخول الأجنبي ومغادرته المملكة، الجوازات والتأشيرات، بطاقات الترانزيت والتنقل الداخلي، كفالة الأجنبي، الحجاج والمطوفين (م1-م31، ويشمل المادة المضافة 5 مكرر).
رخصة الإقامة الدائمة والمؤقتة، سحبها وتجديدها، رسومها، البيانات الواجب تضمينها، شمولها لأفراد الأسرة (م32-م42).
شروط الإقامة بحسب صفة القادم (عمل مؤقت، عمل بلا عقد سابق، تجارة/استثمار، مجاورة الحرمين، طلب العلم، موظفو المفوضيات) (م43-م49، ويشمل المادتين المضافتين 44 مكرر و49 مكررة).
عقوبات دخول الأجانب والتهريب والتزوير ومخالفات المطوفين وأصحاب العمل، الإلغاء العام للأوامر السابقة، تنفيذ النظام (م50-م65، ويشمل المادة المضافة 62 مكرر).

verification_methodology_note:
Foreigners' Residency Law (نظام الإقامة -- also widely known as the Iqama/Kafala law) -- issued as the Royal (Supreme) Order No. 17/2/25/1337 dated 11/9/1371H (~1951-1952G), per every source checked. 65 base articles across 4 فصول (chapters, NOT أبواب/parts) -- الفصل الأول: الأجنبي القادم من الخارج (Articles 1-31); الفصل الثاني: في الإقامة (32-42); الفصل الثالث: في شروط الإقامة (43-49); الفصل الرابع: في العقوبات (50-65) -- plus 4 confirmed-and-text-verified مكرر (repeated/inserted) articles with recoverable substantive text (5 مكرر, 44 مكرر, 49 مكررة, 62 مكرر), for 69 ingested records total, plus one further confirmed-but-unrecoverable مكرر article (61 مكرر) that is NOT ingested -- see below.

PRIMARY-SOURCE ACCESS (BOE and MOI): laws.boe.gov.sa was searched exhaustively this pass (direct site search-engine queries, site: queries, and folder-listing queries) and does NOT appear to index this law at all under any title checked -- BOE's portal returns only نظام الإقامة المميزة (the 'Premium Residency Law', Royal Decree M/106 dated 10/9/1440H, an entirely distinct and much newer instrument establishing a separate investor/talent long-term residency track, lawId 5e9762df-2b15-4e66-8cdc-aa5200f62042) for every 'residency'-related query tried. This is consistent with this very old (1371H) base law predating BOE's normal digitization pipeline and instead being administered directly by the Ministry of Interior (Jawazat/Passports Directorate) outside BOE's system. laws.boe.gov.sa's live portal was also independently confirmed unreachable via direct curl this pass (connection reset), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this portal. MOI's own site (www.moi.gov.sa) hosts a PDF titled (per its own URL and search-engine-indexed title metadata) 'نظام الإقامة (نظام بالتصديق الملكي العالي رقم 17-2/25/1337 في 11/9/1371هـ)' at moi.gov.sa/wps/wcm/connect/13751500426ff3f7ab90ff884cc5c2ae/iqamaa+system.pdf -- but direct curl this pass hit a connection reset, and the Wayback Machine's only two captures of that exact URL are a dead 404 (2012) and a live-site error page titled 'MOI Support' (30 May 2022) -- NOT the actual PDF bytes. MOI's live portal could not be reached in any form this pass.

BEST-AVAILABLE SOURCE ACTUALLY USED: a widely-circulated compiled document titled 'نظام الإقامة والتعديلات الصادرة عليه' ('The Residency Law and the Amendments Issued to It'), reproducing the full 65-article base text plus an extensive article-by-article amendment log citing dozens of specific Royal Decrees/Orders and Council of Ministers Resolutions from 1373H through 1427H. This exact document was independently located in FOUR separately-hosted forms this pass: (1) a PDF hosted by the National Society for Human Rights (nshr.org.sa/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/...pdf, a state-chartered but non-governmental human-rights body, NOT the primary legislative portal) -- downloaded successfully (346KB, valid PDF, 12 pages) but its embedded CID-keyed Tahoma font extracts as scrambled/garbled Arabic via pdftotext (a font-encoding corruption of exactly the kind already documented elsewhere in this corpus for certain older government-style PDFs -- see e.g. sources/pdpl/ocr/pdpl_arabic_law_ocr_quality_report.md and scripts/extract_pdf_text.py's own warning docstring) -- usable only to structurally confirm the document's own title, its internal '(1/1)' .. '(1/28)' page-footer pagination, and the presence of numbered article markers, NOT for clean body text; (2) mohamah.net (a legal-consultation content site, article dated 25 Sep 2017), a clean HTML transcription whose text preserves the IDENTICAL internal '(1/1)'..'(1/28)' page-footer artifacts found in the NSHR PDF, confirming it is a transcription of that same underlying document rather than an independently-authored summary; (3) rakadvocate.blogspot.com (a law-office blog, also dated 2017), an independent HTML transcription that is byte-for-byte identical to mohamah.net's for every passage spot-checked (including the exact same page-footer artifacts and, notably, the exact same internal decree-citation inconsistency for Article 5 mukarrar documented below); (4) islamport.com's 'al-Mawsu'ah al-Shamilah' text archive (a classical/legal-texts digital library, windows-1256-encoded HTML), independently reproducing at least the closing portion of the identical text verbatim. This four-way agreement (one structurally-confirming official-domain-adjacent PDF, three independently-hosted clean textual transcriptions all agreeing word-for-word with each other and with the PDF's own pagination) gives high confidence that the INGESTED TEXT is a faithful, complete reproduction of the genuine officially-circulated compiled document -- but because the live issuing/administering government domain (MOI) itself could not be reached in any usable form, and BOE does not host this law at all, this track is classified TIER_3 ('official source unreachable, 2+ independent secondaries agree') rather than TIER_1 or TIER_2, per this corpus's four-tier verification taxonomy.

STRUCTURE AND STATUS COUNTS: 65 base articles + 4 recoverable مكرر insertions (5, 44, 49, 62) = 69 ingested records. Of the 65 base articles: 48 اصلية (unamended), 16 معدلة (Articles 14, 16, 25, 31, 35, 38, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 52, 53, 56, 60, 61 -- each amendment's specific decree/resolution citation is carried in that article's own history[]), and 1 ملغاة (Article 37, repealed by Royal Decree M/48 dated 10/10/1391H; its last-known pre-repeal text is PRESERVED here, not deleted, per this corpus's binding trust constraint against silently deleting repealed articles). The 4 مكرر insertions are all مضافة (added) and their full substantive text was recovered from the sources above. Article 56's current text is a three-part (أ/ب/ج) provision reflecting a single 1377H amendment (Council of Ministers Resolution 59) to what had previously been a single unlettered paragraph.

ARTICLE 61 MUKARRAR -- CONFIRMED TO EXIST, TEXT NOT RECOVERED, NOT INGESTED: the compiled source document itself records, in its amendment appendix, that Royal Decree M/56 dated 4/9/1427H (ratifying Council of Ministers Resolution 221 dated 2/9/1427H) added a new article numbered '61 مكرر' -- but nowhere in any of the four sources checked (nor in a further two dedicated web searches for this specific article's substantive text) is that article's actual wording reproduced; the compiled document logs only the fact and date of its addition, not its content. Per this corpus's binding trust constraint against fabricating or guessing article text, Article 61 mukarrar is NOT included in this track's articles{} inventory; its confirmed existence and the gap in its recoverable text are recorded in known_unresolved_discrepancies (key residency_article61_mukarrar_text_not_recovered) as an explicit follow-up item rather than silently omitted without disclosure.

OTHER GENERAL (NON-ARTICLE-SPECIFIC) HISTORICAL NOTES found in the compiled source and NOT modeled as per-article amendments (since they do not alter any single numbered article's own text): a Council of Ministers Resolution (166, 12/7/1421H) on employer/expatriate-worker-relationship rules; a Ministerial Resolution (4419, 8/4/1427H) permitting Omani nationals to enter/exit using national ID cards without passport stamping; a fee-treatment clause for expatriate workers' family visas per Royal Decree M/7 (30/2/1419H); and a sponsorship-transfer fee provision per Royal Decree M/43 (2/7/1405H, the same omnibus fee-adjustment decree that also amended Articles 35, 38, and 61). These are noted here for completeness but are not separately ingested as articles.

REPEAL/PREDECESSOR: Article 64 itself states a GENERAL repeal clause -- 'this Law repeals all orders and instructions issued on the subject of residency and foreigners before its issuance' (يلغي هذا النظام العمل بجميع الأوامر والتعليمات الصادرة في موضوع الإقامة والأجانب قبل صدوره) -- WITHOUT naming any single specific predecessor law/decree by number. No source checked identifies a single specific named predecessor 'residency law' that this one replaced (consistent with 1371H being one of the Kingdom's earliest post-unification administrative statutes on this subject), and this corpus does not currently contain any earlier residency-law track for this general repeal clause to attach to. Treated as a confirmed general (non-specific) repeal, not a specific-predecessor repeal.

DISTINCTNESS FROM OTHER CORPUS TRACKS: this law is the general administrative/immigration-status statute (entry/exit, sponsorship/kafala, residency permits, and iqama-violation penalties) -- distinct from this corpus's already-ingested anti_trafficking_law (criminalizes labor exploitation) and labor_law (employment terms), which govern different subject matter entirely.

COMPANION INSTRUMENTS IDENTIFIED, NOT INGESTED THIS PASS (one-law-per-pass rule): (1) نظام الإقامة المميزة (the Premium/Distinguished Residency Law, Royal Decree M/106, 10/9/1440H -- a fully separate, much newer investor/talent long-term residency instrument, the ONLY 'residency' law actually indexed on BOE, lawId 5e9762df-2b15-4e66-8cdc-aa5200f62042) -- NOT ingested as of this original pass; since resolved, this law is now ingested as this corpus's own separate premium_residency track (see sources/premium_residency/law/official_source/premium_residency_law_official_source.json) -- and its own Implementing Regulation, which per that now-ingested track's own known_unresolved_discrepancies remains uningested (only a paraphrased secondary summary was found, not a verbatim text); (2) نظام الجوازات السفرية (the Passports Law, cross-referenced by this law's own compiled amendment appendix for entry/exit visa fees -- already separately flagged as its own coverage-gap candidate in this corpus's reports/coverage_gap_map); (3) a set of Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development / Ministry of Interior rules on exit-re-entry visas and the Muqeem online residency-management system, referenced in passing by secondary sources but not part of this law's own text. None of these are ingested here; all are flagged as follow-up candidates.

No legal wording is altered beyond (a) collapsing incidental double-space artifacts and a residual non-breaking space from HTML transcription, and (b) normalizing two inconsistently-applied, spurious diacritic renderings of the single recurring word 'نظام' (النِظام with a floating kasra under the nun, and نظَام with a floating fatha over the dhad-alif) to the plain, undiacritized 'نظام' -- a full diacritic-frequency scan of the entire source text confirmed these two renderings are the ONLY anomalous/inconsistent diacritics anywhere in the document (every other diacritic found -- tanween, shadda, damma-on-hamza -- is standard, meaningful Arabic orthography on other words and was left untouched). Also normalized: one stray unmatched opening parenthesis in Article 53's text (no matching close anywhere in the sentence -- a transcription artifact, not part of the substantive wording); the decree-citation preamble embedded inline before Article 5 mukarrar's operative text ('صدر مرسوم الملكي ... وهذا نصها:') was excluded from the ingested article text and moved into that article's history[] instead, since it is metadata about the amendment, not the amendment's own operative wording; and Article 37's inline bracketed repeal note was likewise excluded from the ingested (preserved, pre-repeal) article text and is instead carried via legal_status_ar=ملغاة and history[]. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation was performed on the Arabic text (English text in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en is for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Exhaustive site-search and site:-restricted queries against laws.boe.gov.sa found NO entry for this base 1371H Foreigners' Residency Law under any title tried -- BOE's portal appears to index only نظام الإقامة المميزة (the unrelated, much newer 'Premium Residency Law', M/106, 1440H) for every 'residency'-related query attempted this pass; BOE's live portal was also independently confirmed unreachable via direct curl (connection reset), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this portal. The Ministry of Interior's own hosted copy (moi.gov.sa/.../iqamaa+system.pdf, per its own search-engine-indexed title metadata) could not be reached live (connection reset) nor recovered via the Wayback Machine (its only two captures are a dead 404 from 2012 and a live-site HTML error page titled 'MOI Support' from 30 May 2022 -- not the PDF itself). This track is therefore built from the best-available cross-verified secondary reproduction of the officially-circulated compiled document (see verification_methodology_note) and classified TIER_3, not TIER_1/TIER_2, precisely because the issuing/administering government domain could not itself be reached in any usable form this pass.

The adding instrument for Article 5 mukarrar is cited THREE different ways within the SAME compiled source document (confirmed present, identically, in both independent HTML transcriptions checked -- mohamah.net and rakadvocate.blogspot.com -- so this is not a single transcriber's error but an inconsistency in the underlying original compiled document itself): (1) inline, within Article 5 mukarrar's own text, as 'Royal Decree No. M/4 dated 18/7/1393H, per Council of Ministers Resolution No. 484 dated 16/7/1393H'; (2) in the source's own amendment appendix, as 'Royal Decree No. M/40 dated 18/7/1393H, per Council of Ministers Resolution No. 884 dated 16/7/1393H' (same date, different decree number M/40 vs M/4, and different resolution number 884 vs 484); (3) in a second, separate mention later in that same appendix, again as 'Royal Decree No. M/40' but with a DIFFERENT date, 18/7/1394H (one hijri year later than citations 1 and 2). This track does not attempt to silently pick or fabricate a single correct reading; the operative article TEXT itself (which is what is actually ingested) is identical and stable across all citations and all sources checked -- only the identifying decree/resolution number and exact date of the ADDING instrument are internally inconsistent in the best-available source. This article's history[] entry records the majority reading (M/40, 18/7/1393H, Resolution 884) while flagging the two-way decree-number conflict and one-year date conflict here explicitly; a dedicated follow-up check of the Umm Al-Qura Gazette archive for 1393H/1394H could potentially resolve this but was not pursued this pass per this corpus's instruction not to chase every last discrepancy exhaustively.

The compiled source's amendment appendix, while discussing Article 52's SECOND amendment (by Royal Decree M/53 dated 26/9/1392H), literally reads '...بتعديل صدر المادة (5) المعدلة' ('...amending the opening of Article (5) as amended') -- i.e. it names Article (5), not Article (52), even though the surrounding context is entirely about Article 52's amendment history (Article 5 itself was already fully covered earlier, in its own separate section, and has no recorded second amendment anywhere in this source). This is almost certainly a numeral transcription/typo in the source ('5' for '52') given the surrounding context, but this track does not silently correct it without disclosure -- this article's history[] entry quotes the source's literal '(5)' wording alongside this note rather than silently substituting '(52)'.

The compiled source document's amendment appendix confirms that Royal Decree M/56 dated 4/9/1427H (ratifying Council of Ministers Resolution 221 dated 2/9/1427H) added a new article numbered '61 mukarrar' to this Law -- but its actual substantive text is not reproduced anywhere in any of the four independently-checked sources (the NSHR PDF, mohamah.net, rakadvocate.blogspot.com, or islamport.com), nor was it recovered via two additional dedicated web searches targeting this specific article's text. Per this corpus's binding trust constraint against fabricating or guessing article text, Article 61 mukarrar is NOT included in this track's articles{} inventory (which is why the article_count below is 69, not 70) -- its confirmed existence, adding-decree citation, and this recovery gap are disclosed here rather than silently omitted. Flagged as a follow-up item: a dedicated search of the Umm Al-Qura Gazette archive for Royal Decree M/56 (1427H) would be the most direct path to recovering this article's actual text.

Article 64 states only a GENERAL repeal clause ('this Law repeals all orders and instructions issued on the subject of residency and foreigners before its issuance') without naming any single specific predecessor law/decree by number or date. No source checked this pass identifies a specific named prior 'residency law' that this 1371H (1951-1952G) statute replaced, consistent with this being one of the Kingdom's earliest post-unification administrative statutes on this subject (predating even most of this corpus's oldest already-ingested tracks). This corpus does not currently contain any earlier residency-law track for this general repeal clause to attach to. Treated as a confirmed negative finding (general, non-specific repeal only), not an unresolved research gap.

The National Society for Human Rights' own hosted PDF of this exact compiled document (nshr.org.sa/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/...pdf) extracts as scrambled/garbled Arabic via pdftotext -- its embedded CID-keyed 'Tahoma' fonts appear to use a non-standard glyph-to-Unicode mapping, a font-encoding corruption pattern already documented elsewhere in this corpus for other older government-style PDFs (see sources/pdpl/ocr/pdpl_arabic_law_ocr_quality_report.md and the docstring warning in scripts/extract_pdf_text.py). This PDF was used only to structurally confirm the compiled document's title, its 65-article/4-فصل structure, and its internal '(1/1)'..'(1/28)' page-footer pagination (which matches the two independent clean-HTML transcriptions exactly) -- it was NOT used as a source of actual Arabic body text, consistent with this corpus's established practice of treating garbled PDF extractions as non-canonical.
